description:
GH #297. One change, three parts, all reading one constant TUPLE_LANE_BUDGET = 8 (semantic.rs).
1. ShapeDemand::normalize turns a field reading that asks for more lanes than the budget into Whole. This is what fz-rba.1 and fz-rba.2 needed: the first spike collapsed the layout in transport only, while the demand stayed fields(ignore, whole, ...); producers left the ignored fields absent and the whole tuple could not be materialized (proven by backend dump on matrix::ast_eval at budget 4). With the bound in the demand a producer is never told it may leave a field of a whole-travelling tuple unbuilt, and closures in a wide tuple escape first-class.
2. decomposed_field_tys (jobs/transport.rs) is the one answer for a Whole demand on an exact tuple type: field types while the lanes (nested tuples included) fit, otherwise none and the layout is one value lane. tuple_refined_demand, joined_tuple_structural, layout_from_demand and the TransportRecipe::Tuple arm read it.
3. collect_entry_callsite_needs (executable_facts.rs) asks for ExecutableNeed::TupleFields only inside the budget (was fz-rba.5).
The bound is per demand level: a field reading within the budget whose Whole leaves each expand within the budget can reach about budget squared lanes; it is not a strict total.
Signal: unit tests in semantic_test.rs and transport_test.rs; fixtures 01230-01232 (Elixir-checked, three paths); budget-4 stress run of the fixture matrix 3203 passed; at budget 8 no pin moved. wide5000 run 2.26 s to 0.09 s, chain60 1.90 s to 1.20 s (debug, opt-level 1).
Not removed: tuple_refined_demand stays (it now reads decomposed_field_tys); its removal is fz-rba.4.
title: One function decides how a tuple travels
